page: Amazon Web Services i4g.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Driven by the 64-bit ARM architecture, it features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs via an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The CPU architecture incorporates 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic operations. The system provides 32.0 GB of memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a bundled 937 GB local NVMe SSD. Network capability is provisioned at a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the server includes no GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations reveal that the instance provides moderate single-threaded performance alongside constrained multi-threaded execution. Synthetic CPU assessments through stress-ng show an average single-core output of 1520.08, whereas multi-core throughput of 6056.47 places it within the bottom 25th percentile. Geekbench testing mirrors this profile with single-core scores of 969.0 and multi-core scores of 3224.0. Sustained memory bandwidth remains balanced, delivering 71.67 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 34.86 GB/sec for writes. Application-level metrics recorded 4.77 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 4.82 GB/sec in static web serving.

The primary architectural advantage of the i4g.xlarge is its bundled high-speed NVMe storage coupled with high memory density per core, which offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for read- and write-heavy disk applications. A noticeable tradeoff is the lower computational capacity on complex algorithmic, compilation, and compression workloads relative to high-clocked alternative architectures. The configuration is optimal for I/O-intensive workloads, including transactional databases, NoSQL data persistence layers, search indexing, and distributed in-memory caching systems.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and driven by the 64-bit ARM architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical vCPUs powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz, equipped with 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 32.0 GB, resulting in an 8.0 GB per core ratio, paired with a bundled 937 GB local NVMe SSD and a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates moderate single-core processing capabilities and stable uncached memory bandwidth, though multi-threaded compute and encryption performance register in lower percentiles. The combination of dense memory and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage provides strong resource efficiency for disk-bound tasks without requiring external block storage. The i4g.xlarge is well tailored for intermediate NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, search indexing, and distributed caching systems.
